answer: The declaration is a wharf header, so 547 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Fingerprints are counted in inlet, thus the distribution is public, and ferrous lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. A farm of 286 pays that 286 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
